day_shape: 67 items: CENTCOM says US forces sank an Iranian tanker in the Gulf of Oman and have redirected 92 vessels under a maritime blockade, IDF strikes on southern Lebanon destroy Ghandour Hospital with Lebanese authorities reporting 7 dead, Netanyahu says 'end of Iranian regime is near', Bessent claims Iran has 30m barrels left for China; nothing from UK Parliament, State Department or OFAC.

threads.label: US maritime blockade and tanker sinking
threads.summary: CENTCOM announced US forces sank an Iranian oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman and posted that F-35As are patrolling as the blockade continues. As of 6 September, CENTCOM said US forces have redirected 92 commercial vessels, disabled 3 and boarded 2; Treasury Secretary Bessent told Fox News Iran has about 30 million barrels left uncommitted to China.

threads.label: IDF strikes southern Lebanon, hospital destroyed
threads.summary: The IDF said it struck Hezbollah weapons stores, infrastructure and a command centre inside a former hospital in southern Lebanon in response to a drone attack on troops near Ali Taher Ridge. Lebanese health authorities reported 4 dead and 20 wounded by morning, rising to 7 after a further drone strike on a vehicle in Nabatieh; Defa Press and Berri said Israel is violating the ceasefire.

threads.label: Netanyahu regime-fall message and IDF readiness drill
threads.summary: Netanyahu said 'the end of the Iranian regime is near' and that its fall would 'change the fate of the Middle East'. The IDF said Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir ordered a surprise multi-front readiness exercise for General Headquarters; Jerusalem Post opinion pieces framed IRGC pressure and Iranian street unrest.

threads.label: IRGC internal security operations
threads.summary: Defa Press and IRIB reported IRGC intelligence in Fars arrested an eight-member 'armed counter-revolutionary' network linked to a royalist faction, and announced arrests near Karaj of people in a motorcade attributed to the MEK. Defa Press also reported a border-guard interdiction of 'security-threat items' at Ashno in West Azerbaijan and remarks from the border-guard commander vowing no infiltration.

threads.label: Iraq, US withdrawal and Hormuz coordination
threads.summary: Defa Press quoted the Iraqi PM saying US air-defence systems and remaining forces will withdraw from Iraqi Kurdistan by end of September, and cited an Iraqi parliamentary commission member on Baghdad-Tehran coordination for tanker passage through the Strait of Hormuz. A Jerusalem Post analysis said a US withdrawal could leave Iraqi Kurds exposed to militias and Iranian attack.

threads.label: West Bank raid and Palestinian politics
threads.summary: The IDF, Shin Bet and Yamam said they dismantled a 10-member Hamas cell in Aqqaba near Nablus, seizing a rocket, an M16 and explosives from a weapons cache. Jerusalem Post also reported Fatah's Jibril Rajoub met Hamas leaders in Turkey ahead of planned Palestinian elections.

threads.label: Yemen strikes on Saudi targets
threads.summary: IRIB and Defa Press carried Yemen Armed Forces claims of downing a Saudi Wing Loong 2 drone north-west of Taiz and of a ballistic missile strike on a gathering of Saudi-allied commanders. Jerusalem Post reported the Houthis said they targeted Saudi-linked vehicles with 'domestically manufactured' ballistic missiles.

events.title_en: Iraq parliament oil and gas commission: Strait of Hormuz is Iraq's 'economic lung'. Coordination between Tehran and Baghdad continues for safe passage of Iraqi tankers through the Strait of Hormuz
events.summary_en: Iraq parliament oil and gas commission: Strait of Hormuz is Iraq's 'economic lung'. Coordination between Tehran and Baghdad continues for safe passage of Iraqi tankers through the Strait of Hormuz. Qaisar Al-Jowrani, member of Iraq's parliament oil and gas commission, announced coordination between Baghdad and Tehran for safe passage of Iraqi tankers through the Strait of Hormuz. The Strait of Hormuz is recognised as Iraq's 'economic lung' and coordination with Tehran is in place for tanker passage and exports to global markets via this route. Continued flow of exports through maritime routes and preservation of navigation stability in the Strait of Hormuz are vital for protecting Iraq's economy and ensuring public revenues.

In this context, closure of the Strait of Hormuz for a small and weak country like Qatar, as the world's second-largest liquefied natural gas (LNG) exporter, has created significant problems and imposed an unprecedented energy crisis on the world.
